title: Hidden PowerShell loader (monkey.png steganography) compiles Add-Type payloads and opens LSASS with full access on scranton
rationale: All describe the same LSASS-access action by PowerShell-family processes attributable to pbeesly: hidden PowerShell PID 2976 on scranton opened lsass.exe with 0x1f3fff/0x1fffff and UNKNOWN call-trace frames, plus the lower-privilege 0x1000 opens and the wsmprovhost LSASS open on nashua. The csc.exe Add-Type compiles from the same hidden loader are part of this action chain. Best fit is LSASS Memory (T1003.001); no dump file was written, hence suspicious.

title: Hands-on-keyboard credential-access toolkit in pbeesly's PowerShell session on scranton (discovery, accesschk, private-key export, screen capture, exfil staging)
rationale: Single finding describing the combined hands-on-keyboard session; the umbrella Input Capture technique (T1056) is the best single fit for the session that includes screen capture and keystroke collection alongside other credential tooling.

title: Get-Keystrokes keylogger job on scranton
rationale: Get-Keystrokes background job launched, viewed and removed is keylogging.

title: Screen capture loop (Invoke-ScreenCapture) on scranton
rationale: Invoke-ScreenCapture background job writing .bmp screenshots of the desktop is GUI input capture.

title: WebDAV/UNC forced-authentication channel used to exfiltrate OfficeSupplies.7z to 192.168.0.4
rationale: Both describe the same Invoke-Exfil action mapping \\192.168.0.4\webdav and copying the archive; the WebDAV/UNC forced-authentication channel is T1187.

title: Credential-adjacent file harvesting and archiving on scranton and nashua
rationale: Both describe the same collection action: enumerating user files matching *pass*/*psw*/*login*/*admin*/*vpn* patterns and archiving them (Draft.Zip on scranton, working.zip on nashua).

title: Plaintext password on PsExec command line to NASHUA; accesschk passwordsDB on scranton
rationale: Both describe credentials in files/command lines: accesschk writing passwordsDB and PsExec64 run with '-p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by' against NASHUA.

title: Private keys packed into 7z and pushed to attacker WebDAV
rationale: Invoke-Exfil compressing Downloads containing the exported .pfx keys and copying to the WebDAV share is theft of private keys (T1552.004).

title: GptTmpl.inf read from NEWYORK sysvol by external hosts and GroupPolicy DataStore writes
rationale: Reading the SYSVOL security-template GptTmpl.inf is Group Policy Preferences credential access (T1552.006).

title: hostui.exe elevated via runas from PowerShell on scranton
rationale: Elevation via runas from PowerShell; assessed under Group Policy Preferences (T1552.006) at low confidence.

title: Get-PrivateKeys certificate export treated as credential-store access on scranton
rationale: Same Get-PrivateKeys action; grouped separately as the credential-store access characterization (T1555).

title: Get-PrivateKeys .pfx export characterized as Windows Credential Manager access
rationale: Same Get-PrivateKeys action; the finding characterizes it as credential-store access (T1555.004).

title: sdclt.exe UAC-bypass pattern preceding Add-Type compile on scranton
rationale: sdclt.exe launches following HKCU Folder shell open command writes; assessed as Modify Authentication Process (T1556) at low confidence.

title: No SAML token forgery; certificate private keys exported for theft
rationale: Finding explicitly reports no SAML token forging but the Get-PrivateKeys export; the observed action is certificate private-key theft, assessed under the SAML-token hypothesis as negative.

title: Certificate private-key export (Get-PrivateKeys) to .pfx on scranton
rationale: Same Get-PrivateKeys action exporting LocalMachine certificate private keys to password-protected .pfx files; best fit is Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates (T1649).
